newsitem.title: UK: General Accident buoyed by U.S. strength.
newsitem.headline: General Accident buoyed by U.S. strength.

text.p: Shares in insurance group General Accident Plc rose on Monday, buoyed by strength in the U.S. bond and equity markets and following positive comments from brokers, traders said.
Broker Kleinwort Benson said it had raised its asset value estimates and reiterated its "buy" stance on the stock.

"The strength in equities markets has surpassed our previous estimates for the year, and in the light of U.S. figures last week we're now taking a less bearish stance on bonds," said Oliver Steel, insurance specialist at Kleinwort Benson.
Kleinwort said their asset value estimates had risen to 711p for the end of 1996, and to around 800p for the end of 1997. Comparative estimates were not immediately available.
Pretax profit forecasts remain unchanged at 415 million stg for 1996 and 450 million stg for 1997, the broker said.
"General Accident has a substantial block of their investments in U.S. bonds and equities," added Steel.
U.S. equity and bond markets surged on Friday after a modest rise in U.S. consumer prices and a continuing slowdown in retail sales eased fears of a possible interest rate rise.
